facts.text: Past Holden Lake the path can vanish into avalanche debris in early July; keeping to the right-hand (north) trail on the way to the pass avoids a swampy wade.
On the way down in July, the waterfall slabs below the glacier are slippery wherever wet and some steps have piton anchors for a short rappel; belaying across the moat at the glacier edge is common.

facts.text: In late July the downclimb from the knife-edge off the West Summit to the summit block was very exposed with few holds, about 5.3, and the summit block took three roped low-5th pitches.
In late July the Mary Green Glacier was broken but the entry had no moat; two crevasse crossings in evening soft snow, then the waterfall ledges downclimbed.
One party reached the Dark Peak side from the PCT at Hemlock Camp instead, straight up the steep woods to Dark Fin Col, avoiding the Swamp Creek brush; flat bivy spots at the col are scarce.

notes: The catalog has no standard Mary Green Glacier route (all recordings and ~170 July ascents follow it; main-summit pin on the NE Buttress route is within 0-10 m of every track). Summit pins on Soviet/Oregonian/Cascadian sit on the Southwest Peak (~560 m from the main summit), consistent with those routes finishing there. No track assigned because none is a recording of one of these five routes. NE Buttress facts cover only the Holden Pass approach and the shared glacier descent. July 2026 reports note Holden Village was inaccessible after storm damage, a one-off I left out.
